A solid circular shaft of uniform diameter d is subjected to a pure torque T = 1,000,000 N·mm over its full length L = 1500 mm.
The material is 6061-T6 aluminum with shear modulus G = 25939.8 MPa (N/mm²).
The design constraint is that the total angle of twist over the 1500 mm length must not exceed φ_allow = 0.75° = 0.01308997 rad.
The governing relation is the linear-elastic torsion formula φ = TL/(JG), where J = πd⁴/32 for a solid circular cross-section.
Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic behavior, no bending, no transverse shear force, and a prismatic (constant-diameter) shaft.
Determine the minimum solid shaft diameter d_min by solving d⁴ ≥ 32TL/(π·φ_allow·G) and reporting the result in millimeters.
State the computed value of J at d_min, the resulting maximum shear stress τ_max = T·r/J = 16T/(πd³) at the outer fiber, and confirm that the twist at d_min equals φ_allow.
Present all governing equations, the algebraic solution for d, and the final numerical answer rounded to one decimal place.
